jobs.description: Join our dynamic Data Center Engineering Operations Team and become a critical architect of the infrastructure that powers global cloud computing. You'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of Amazon Web Services' physical infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that support millions of customers worldwide. The Data Center Chief Engineer (CE) is responsible for ensuring that all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating at peak efficiency. This involves planned preventative maintenance of equipment, daily corrective work, and emergency response. The CE serves as an expert technical resource interacting with onsite Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT) and any third-party vendors. They are expected to be a singular focal point for all facility operations within a given data center and to support AWS. AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help. You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion. NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role. NOTE: Relocation assistance will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position. Key job responsibilities - Act as the primary escalation point for all facilities-related issues. Oversee operation and management of routine and emergency services on a variety of critical systems such as switchgear, generators, UPS systems, power distribution equipment, chillers, cooling towers, computer room air handlers, building monitoring systems, etc. - Perform root cause analysis of equipment failures and troubleshooting of facility within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA). - Provide training and guidance to Engineering Operations Technicians and are responsible for working with Facility Manager (FM) to set team culture. - Create and deploy new standard practices for Engineering Operations Technicians, Chief Engineers, and vendor support teams - May assist in the building out of new facilities and assist in projects to increase current facility efficiency - Working outside of normal business hours for routine maintenance as required, including responding to out-of-hours emergency calls. - Communicate complex technical information to a non-technical audience. - Work with IT managers and other business leaders to coordinate projects, manage capacity, and optimize plant safety, performance, reliability and efficiency - Ensure all safety procedures are adhered to by vendor and Amazon staff - Establish building performance benchmarks, conduct analyses, and prepare reports on all aspects of the critical facility of operations and maintenance. - Utilize Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook and other basic administrative tools to perform day-to-day tasks - Serve as the on-site fire protection subject matter expert (SME) and single point of contact for the local Fire Marshall, building a strong working relationship to support timely Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (TCO) issuance and rack handoffs. - Establish and maintain the baseline standard for site-wide fire safety, ensuring all fire detection, suppression, and monitoring systems remain fully operational. - Plan and lead bi-annual fire drills across all facilities and set the standard for site-wide fire safety training. - Serve as the SME and single point of contact for all operations, safety, and compliance matters within the Ancillary Water Building (AWB). - Establish operating standards and oversee monitoring, compliance, and training for the Ancillary Water Building (AWB) to ensure safe, reliable operation. Physical Requirements: - Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodation: - Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently - Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds - Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder - Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position - Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection Essential Requirements: - Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed - Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational - Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

jobs.description: Amazon LEO is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Amazon LEO will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity. The Antenna Test Infrastructure team develops the technology, systems, and chambers that validate LEO hardware across both Satellite and Customer Terminal programs. We design and build the mechanical infrastructure — test fixtures, handling tools, and RF chambers — that enable high-fidelity antenna characterization at production scale. In this role, you will serve as the senior mechanical engineering lead for tooling and chamber design within the team. You will own the full design lifecycle of test fixtures, assembly tooling, and RF chamber mechanical systems — from concept development and trade studies through detailed design, fabrication, and commissioning. You will drive GD&T rigor, lead design reviews, and ensure that every fixture and chamber meets demanding RF, thermal, and dimensional requirements. This is a hands-on technical leadership role: you will set the mechanical design standard for the team while project-managing complex builds across internal manufacturing partners and external vendors. Export Control Requirement Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities - Lead the mechanical design of RF OTA test chambers, including structural enclosures, positioner mounts, DUT fixturing, cable routing, and access panel integration, ensuring designs meet RF performance, thermal stability, and dimensional accuracy requirements. - Design and detail test fixtures, assembly tooling, and ergonomic handling aids for Satellite and Customer Terminal components and products across all stages of integration and test. - Apply rigorous GD&T and perform tolerance stackup analyses to guarantee fit, function, and repeatability across multi-part fixture assemblies and chamber mechanical interfaces. - Perform structural and thermal FEA to validate fixture and chamber designs prior to fabrication, iterating on geometry, material selection, and load paths to meet performance and safety margins. - Create and release production-quality 2D drawings, 3D models, and BOMs in NX/Teamcenter; own document control processes and maintain configuration management for all tooling and chamber hardware. - Lead part design reviews and peer reviews, establishing and enforcing mechanical design standards across the team. - Develop and execute CMM inspection plans and first-article inspection (FAI) reports; operate or direct the operation of CMMs, laser trackers, and optical measurement systems to verify critical dimensions, alignments, and fixture repeatability. - Define metrology strategies for chamber alignment verification, positioner accuracy characterization, and ongoing calibration of mechanical test infrastructure. - Project-manage RF chamber design and build efforts end-to-end: scope definition, requirements capture, budgeting, scheduling, vendor selection, design review gates, and commissioning. - Collaborate with RF, thermal, and systems engineering teams to translate test requirements into mechanical specifications and ensure chamber and fixture designs do not compromise electromagnetic or thermal performance. - Coordinate with internal machine shops and external fabrication vendors on manufacturability, material procurement, and build schedules for custom capital equipment.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the team
Within GTM, the Partner Enablement team builds the programs, credentials, and learning infrastructure that allow Anthropic's ecosystem of system integrators, cloud providers, resellers, and technology partners to build deep Claude expertise and deliver successful customer outcomes at scale. We work cross-functionally across Partnerships, Sales, Applied AI, Product, Marketing, and Legal to make sure partner-facing programs are clear, consistent, and high-impact.
About the role
Anthropic is launching a global reseller program, and we are looking for a Reseller Enablement Lead to build the enablement motion that makes it work. You will design and launch reseller certification, training, and readiness programs alongside the program itself, starting in our first launch markets and scaling globally from there.
This is a build-and-run role. In the first months you will stand up the foundation from scratch: what a reseller needs to know to sell Claude well, how we certify that they know it, and how we deliver that across markets and languages. From there, you will own the motion as it grows, evolving content and modalities as the program's commercial structure matures, localizing for new regions, and using enablement to keep partner behavior aligned with how we want Claude sold.
You will be the single global owner for reseller enablement, scaling delivery through training networks rather than a large direct team. This is a highly cross-functional role working closely with Partnerships, Partner Programs, Partner Operations, Sales, Applied AI, and Certification to ensure reseller-facing programs land clearly and drive measurable outcomes.
Responsibilities
Define and own Anthropic's reseller enablement strategy, from launch in initial markets through global rollout
Own delivery of the message you build: present and deliver training directly to reseller sellers and leaders, and activate training partners so they carry it consistently at scale
Build the reseller curriculum and certification path from the ground up, covering commercial mechanics, program rules, platform and product fundamentals, and responsible use
Design repeatable programs across partner onboarding, sales readiness, recertification, and product launches, choosing modalities that fit how reseller sellers actually learn and what motivates them
Stand up localized delivery in launch markets, then extend the model to new regions through training networks and regional enablement teams
Work closely with Applied AI to translate technical concepts into clear, digestible content on Anthropic's models and products for a seller audience
Evolve enablement as the program evolves, keeping content current with changes to commercial structure, transaction rails, and program requirements
Use enablement as a governance lever, building content and reinforcement that keeps partner selling behavior on program and addresses drift when it appears
Enable Anthropic sellers and partner managers to co-sell and engage effectively with resellers
Partner cross-functionally with Partner Programs, Partner Operations, and Sales to align priorities and ensure consistent execution
Establish metrics and reporting to track reseller certification, activation, and contribution to registered pipeline and consumption
Build feedback loops that bring reseller insights back into program design, enablement, and GTM strategy
You may be a good fit if you
Have 7-10+ years of experience across partner enablement, partner programs, product marketing, with a clear track record of designing and owning programs end to end. Channel and Alliances experience is key, but must be accompanied with demonstrated program ownership.
Understand how resell and channel ecosystems work commercially, including deal registration, margin and rebate structures, partner tiering, and cloud marketplace motions
Have built and scaled partner enablement or certification programs from nothing to something in a high-growth technology environment
Think operationally and in systems, designing for scale across regions and languages rather than one-off efforts
Understand how to package enablement: which modality fits which audience, what motivates partner sellers, and how to structure a curriculum that produces real selling capability
Are a strong presenter and facilitator, able to deliver training credibly to partner audiences and equip others to deliver it the same way
Combine leadership and hands-on execution, equally comfortable setting strategy with executives and building the first version of a course yourself
Bring executive presence with partner and internal leadership, and the scrappiness to get things done in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment
Are an effective cross-functional operator who can drive alignment across complex organizations
Strong candidates may also have
Experience launching programs in a single region and then scaling them globally, including localization and in-market delivery
Experience building or running an authorized training partner or certified instructor network
Prior ownership of, or close partnership with, a technology certification program
Experience with resell motions in Japan, Korea, or other reseller-led markets
A track record connecting enablement activity to pipeline and revenue outcomes

Your safety matters to us.

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic's Go-To-Market team is growing quickly, and every new Account Executive, BDR, and GTM teammate we hire needs to become productive, confident, and credible on Claude faster than at any other company. The GTM Onboarding program is one way that happens. It's the first experience new hires have of how we sell, who our customers are, what our products do, and how we work together — and it sets the trajectory for their ramp.
We're looking for someone to own that program end to end. You'll design and run recurring onboarding cohorts for new GTM hires: building the curriculum, coordinating facilitators from across Sales, Marketing, Applied AI, and Product, running live sessions, and making sure every cohort leaves ready to have real customer conversations. This person will be the front door to GTM. You will set the tone for new hires’ first impression of Anthropic and our team.
You'll also own what happens after onboarding ends. That means measuring ramp, tracking attendance and comprehension, gathering feedback, and using what you learn to improve the next cycle. You'll build and maintain the operational machinery behind the program — rosters, calendars, facilitator communications, mock discovery calls — and you'll use Claude itself to automate as much of it as possible.
This is a highly cross-functional role. You'll partner with GTM leadership, hiring managers, Revenue Operations, Marketing, and product teams to keep the program current as our products and sales motions evolve. You’ll work closely with subject matter experts, but you'll need to be a generalist who can help new hires connect the dots and build robust mental models for how the business operates.
This role reports into the GTM Enablement team.
Key responsibilities
Own the GTM Onboarding program end to end: curriculum design, cohort scheduling, facilitator coordination, live delivery, and continuous improvement
Design and deliver training that makes Anthropic's products, sales motions, customer stories, and tools (Salesforce, Gong, Apollo, and others) accessible to sellers from a range of backgrounds
Serve as an extension to subject matter experts on Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, and the Claude Developer Platform for new GTM hires, and keep onboarding content accurate as products change
Recruit, prepare, and support a rotating bench of internal facilitators and field volunteers, including briefing them on each cohort's composition and running mock discovery calls with new AEs
Build and maintain the program's operational infrastructure — rosters, calendar logistics, and communications — and automate recurring work using Claude
Measure program effectiveness through attendance, comprehension checks, feedback surveys, and ramp metrics, and present findings and recommendations to GTM leadership
Build and maintain 30/60/90 day ramp plans and post-onboarding resources that carry new hires from cohort to quota
Partner with hiring managers, Revenue Operations, Marketing, and product teams to identify enablement gaps and incorporate new content into the program
Work with the global enablement team to adapt and extend the program for international GTM teams and new role types as the organization grows

Experience in sales enablement, and/or program management-related roles
Have designed and delivered onboarding or training programs for sales teams, including building curriculum and facilitating live sessions

Bring strong program management skills, with a track record of running recurring, multi-stakeholder operations reliably

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
At Anthropic, we believe new AI capabilities are best achieved through secure foundations, not in spite of them. As capabilities grow more advanced, it is critical that progress moves forward safely and for the benefit of all society. It is the reason why security sits at the center of our work, and not as an afterthought.
We're specifically looking for a Software Engineer to help us build and maintain new agentic coding tools for developers. The ideal candidate will have a passion for developer tools, extensive knowledge of diverse programming environments and languages, and experience with advanced LLM features like tool-use, chaining and orchestration patterns, and prompt engineering. Curiosity about AI research is a must!

Design, build, and maintain scalable features and infrastructure for AI-powered development tools

Collaborate with researchers to improve model capabilities through shared tools and evals
Stay ahead of advancements in AI-assisted coding by experimenting with new tools, evaluating emerging techniques, and tracking enhancements to existing ones
Contribute across the stack—from front-end UI to back-end infrastructure—to develop new features, fix bugs, and optimize performance
Dive into possibly unfamiliar areas like Python notebooks, VS Code plug-ins, and containerized environments.
You may be a good fit if you:
Are excited about AI-assisted coding as a tool to enhance developer productivity and creativity—not replace human ingenuity
Spend a lot of time refining and customizing your AI workflows
Have experience building and maintaining dev tools
Are an expert in React development, including performance optimization, modern patterns (hooks, context, suspense), and component architecture
Specialize in user experience engineering but are a capable full stack developer
Have hands-on experience working with large language models and prompt engineering
Have worked on projects with stringent safety, security and/or compliance requirements
Care about the societal impacts and ethics of your work
Have 6+ years of work experience
Strong candidates may also have experience with:
Building and maintaining CLI tools
Working in large codebases and quickly jumping in to unfamiliar development environments
Working with container orchestration and cloud infrastructure
Scaling TypeScript projects
Working with alternate JavaScript runtimes like Bun and Deno

Your safety matters to us.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time.
